title: der, die, das — das Geschlecht der Nomen
summary: German's three noun genders, a few patterns to guess them, and why plurals are all die

blocks.title: Every noun has a gender
blocks.body: German nouns are **der** (masculine), **die** (feminine), or **das** (neuter). It's mostly **grammatical, not logical**: *das Mädchen* (the girl) is neuter, *der Löffel* (spoon) is masculine. So never learn a noun bare — **learn it with its article**: not *Tisch*, but *der Tisch*. Gender also decides next week's endings, when *der* becomes *den* and *dem* — so banking it now pays off.
blocks.callout: Learn "der Tisch", never just "Tisch". The article is part of the word.

blocks.title: Nouns with their articles — tap to hear
Patterns that help you guess
blocks.body: You can't always predict gender, but endings tip you off. Nouns ending in **-ung, -heit, -keit, -tion** are almost always **die** (*die Zeitung*, *die Freiheit*). Any **-chen** or **-lein** word is **das** (*das Brötchen*). Many **-er** words for people and tools are **der** (*der Bäcker*, *der Computer*).

blocks.title: When the ending beats the meaning

pairs.note: Any -chen word is *das*, no matter what it means. Grammar wins.

blocks.title: Plurals: everything becomes die
blocks.body: Good news: **every** plural takes **die**, whatever the singular gender. *der Tisch → die Tische*, *das Kind → die Kinder*, *die Frau → die Frauen*. The ending itself varies (**-e, -er, -n/-en, -s**, sometimes with an umlaut), so learn the plural alongside the word: *der Apfel → die Äpfel*.
blocks.callout: In the plural, der and das both surrender to die.

blocks.explain: *-ung* nouns are feminine → *die Zeitung*. The ending gives it away.
*das Kind* — a child is grammatically neuter. Don't overthink it; just bank it.

blocks.title: der / die / das — repeat after the audio
Point and name it
blocks.prompt: Point at something: 'Das ist …' + the right article + the noun.
Collect five nouns you saw around you today. Write each one with its article — der, die, or das. If you're unsure, guess from the ending, then check.
